To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the transfer, processing and storage of large volumes of data are possible, even with the limited resources that were available at the time.
we successfully transferred 0.5TB per day from Tibet to CERN and back, that we processed the data at CERN using 2000 CPUs, and that we distributed the data back to Tibet.

we have developed a system that is capable of transferring, processing and distributing 0.5TB of raw cosmic ray data per day, and that this system has been successfully demonstrated at the iGrid workshop in November 2005.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following: (1) transfer of cosmic ray data collected by the YBJ-ARGOs experiment from Tibet to the US; (2) processing of those data using a grid-based approach; and (3) distributing processed data to the physicists-users.

the following: (1) The design and implementation of a high speed network to transfer the raw cosmic ray data collected in Tibet to a remote site in Italy; (2) the design and implementation of an efficient and scalable data processing system that can process the stream of data in a timely fashion; (3) the design and development of a web-based data distribution system to make the processed data available to the physicists.
the development and deployment of a high-performance data management system for the YBJ-ARGON experiment.

the system works well, and that the performance meets the expectations of the users.
the system has worked very well and has met the requirements of the experiment.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the YBJ-ARG0 collaboration was successful in transferring, processing and distributing the data at an unprecedented scale.
the YBJ-ARG0 experiment has successfully demonstrated that the data transfer and processing of a high energy astrophysics experiment can be done efficiently with the use of grid technologies.
iGrid 2004 and 2005 provided the opportunity for us to test our data transfer, processing and storage systems.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a distributed computing environment can be successfully deployed to support a data-intensive science project.
a large scale, high speed and high throughput data distribution network can be constructed and operated with commodity hardware and open source software.
the data transfer, processing and storage can be done efficiently and in a timely fashion.
